svg.text: MPx Boil-Loop · Electronics architecture and base layout (preliminary)
One 4S Li-ion bus (12–16.8 V) feeds everything; USB-C PD charges the pack and tops up the bus. Hardware safety cut-offs sit in series with the heaters, independent of firmware.
6 × NTC 10 k B3950 in SS316 probes: tank, H1 out, boil zone, calm zone, HX hot
Calm-zone level: SS pins (conductive) → filter clog alert when level rises
Boil-zone level: SS pins → dry-boil interlock
Tank: capacitive pad on seat (no water contact)
SPI + touch lines to the MCU
tilt switch (or MPU-6050) · hall/reed on top hatch · hatch lock solenoid 12 V
heaters ~49 W · pump ~2.5 W · valve 0 W (latching) · MCU+display ~1.5 W
sensors < 0.1 W · charger loss ~1 W → ~54 W total
warm-up: heaters up to 150 W (100 W from USB + 50 W from pack)
Battery sits low and away from the core, under 45 °C. PCB at the front for the display
harness. USB-C and the vent at the rear.
Heaters run straight off 12–16.8 V with PWM, so there is no big converter in the heater
path. 12 V cartridges give ~40 W at 12 V and ~78 W at 16.8 V; firmware limits the duty to
A 100 W (20 V 5 A, e-marked cable) charger runs steady production with the pack topping
up. 65 W chargers work but warm-up takes longer. PD 3.1 at 140 W is a later option.
Cells and pack must be BIS-registered under IS 16046 (Parts 1 & 2, the Indian adoption of
IEC 62133-2) before sale. ≤ 100 Wh keeps air shipping simple. Requirement 4.2 / 7.2 met by
Two thermostats + two one-shot fuses cut heater power with no firmware involved. Tilt,
open hatch, empty boil zone or watchdog timeout drop the load-switch enable. IEC 60335-1
is the reference for temperature rise and leakage (req 7.6).
Req 7.1 asks IP65 for electronics. The base gets a gasketed PCB tray and conformal coat
(target IP54 for the base, IP65 for the PCB tray); a spill path drains around the base,
Fill → Heat (batch to boil) → Hold τ (valve returns water to tank) → Dispense →
Idle/keep-warm off. Counts litres for filter life and descale, logs temps for the app.
